claims.claim: Consolidated Water links desalination engineering/operations to freshwater scarcity, with long-duration concessions and new plants converting seawater-treatment capability into municipal/island water resilience.

The Hawaii and Florida project pipeline broadens geography beyond legacy Caribbean operations, but a limited notice to proceed is an early execution bridge rather than evidence that the full $204M project economics are secured.

causalEdges: desalination technology -> potable-water supply -> water-scarcity resilience -> human/municipal water need
long-term concession -> operating continuity -> infrastructure reliability
geographic project expansion -> diversified water infrastructure exposure -> reduced single-region dependence

risks.risk: Project-development duration and permitting/authorization stages can delay conversion from identified water need to contracted revenue.

unknowns.unknown: Full Kalaeloa authorization, final economics and construction timing remain contingent on later milestones.

claims.claim: The principal confidence check is conversion: project announcements and limited notices to proceed demonstrate opportunity but not full authorization, revenue timing or margin realization.
Q2 consolidated revenue declined 2% even as bulk revenue rose 20%, so current evidence supports segment strength and future optionality rather than a claim of broad present-day top-line acceleration.

risks.risk: Large-project concentration can create lumpy revenue and execution exposure if major authorizations slip.
Single-source current evidence limits independent confirmation of project progression, although the SEC-filed issuer disclosure is primary and reproducible.

unknowns.unknown: Post-Q2 evidence is needed to verify whether awards have begun converting into broader revenue growth.
